slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you sound
more confident when you talk
End your sentences going down, not up. When your voice rises at the end, everything sounds like a question. Drop the pitch slightly and even simple statements sound sure.
Stop starting with "Sorry, but." Just say the thing. "I think we should try another approach." Apologising before you speak tells people your idea isn't worth their time.
Breathe before you start. One slow breath, then speak. It lowers your voice, slows your pace and stops the rushed, breathless sound that nerves always create.
Look at people when you make your point. Not at the table, not at your phone. Eye contact while you speak makes your words land twice as hard as the exact same words said to the floor.
Cut "just" and "kind of" from your sentences. "I just wanted to kind of check" becomes "I wanted to check." Small words soften everything, and too many make you sound unsure.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. When you know more, you hesitate less, and confident speaking starts with having something real to say.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. When you know more, you hesitate less, and confident speaking gets easy.

slides.texte_overlay: Practice your stories out loud alone. In the car, in the shower. The second time you tell a story, it already sounds smoother. Confident speakers just rehearsed when nobody was watching.
